Roadmap featured wave (pet/activity/knowledge-graph/peek/mirror/lock/scratchpad) is install-time, privacy-default (activity store_command_args:false), same-capability-model-as-core.

(a) SDK/TEMPLATE READINESS GAPS (must land first, in SDK/template repos):
- R-SDK-1: bitty.d.lua LuaLS defs generated/derived from accepted host contract (register_panel/on_event/get_terminal_state + L1/L2 surfaces only); must not invent caps.
- R-SDK-2: manifest schema + bitty-plugin-lint CLI validating plugin.toml against bitty-package acceptance (closed-set caps, compat.bitty/plugin-api ranges, lazy triggers).
- R-SDK-3: mock-host + conformance fixtures (deny-by-default, missing-service, unload/reload, quota/budget, malformed input, version mismatch); mock must NOT be more permissive than host.

1. bitty-plugin-activity (bitty-featured.activity): privacy-first local activity timeline (counts/durations/cwd aggregates, store_command_args:false default, workspace cannot widen). Caps: terminal.semantic-read + store quota. Depends: R-SDK-1/2/3.

3. bitty-plugin-peek: hover/preview anchored to semantic zone/rich block via overlay slot; alternate-screen default-off. Caps: terminal.semantic-read + ui.overlay. Depends: R-SDK-1/2/3.
4. bitty-plugin-pet: companion overlay reacting to observation events (bell/focus/exited), attributable idle budgets. Caps: ui.overlay + observation events. Depends: R-SDK-1/2.
DEFERRED to wave 2 (rationale): mirror (snapshot-versioning risk), lock (interception fail-open + veto determinism), knowledge-graph (service-version multiplicity unresolved OQ), any panel provider (Panel vision CTX-0094 pending), anything needing fs.write/network/process/high-risk caps.

- Review burden: 4 repos x (CI+CodeQL+review) + SDK/template gates; independent reviewer per PR; docs-sync per repo (bitty-docs canonical). Mitigation: sequential wave (activity first as pathfinder), shared template CI.
- Scope creep: panel providers / high-risk caps / network / fs.write must stay out of batch; any request -> new task + RFC, never silent widening.

{"after":{"description":"Priority: P1 | Area: ipc | Labels: fix,area:ipc,P1 | Milestone: v0.1.0 | RFC: OQ-018 | Task: CTX-0320

DEFECT (live e2e campaign, origin/main bbad681): workspace ids are positional in some verbs but sequence-named in list output; they diverge after close+new.

Repro (fresh instance):
  bitty ctl workspace new            -> created ws:2, list names [ws1, ws2]
  bitty ctl workspace new            -> created ws:3, list names [ws1, ws2, ws3]
  bitty ctl workspace close ws:2     -> ok, list names [ws1, ws3]
  bitty ctl workspace new            -> created ws:3, tabline "1:ws1 2:ws3 3:ws4*", list names [ws1, ws3, ws4]
  bitty ctl workspace close ws:4     -> NotFound "no such workspace ws:4"
So `workspace new` reports a positional id (index+1) while the slot's *name* is ws{creation-seq}; `focus`/`close` interpret ws:N as a 1-based position, so the id printed by `new` and `list` cannot be fed back to close/focus.

Root cause: crates/bitty-app/src/ctl/apply.rs:360-365 (created = index+1) vs crates/bitty-runtime/src/runtime/workspaces.rs (name = ws{seq}, next_workspace_seq advances); list returns names, close/focus return/accept positions.
Fix: define one canonical stable workspace id (seq-based) across new/list/focus/close/move.

Evidence: recording/ctx-0320/evidence/fresh-repro-d2.txt, recording/ctx-0320/evidence/ipc-workspace-id-probe.txt
Severity: P1 (scripted workspace management cannot round-trip ids).

{"description":"Priority: P2 | Area: repo-meta | Labels: chore,area:repo-meta,P2 | Milestone: v0.1.0 | RFC: OQ-TBD | Task: CTX-TBD

# Adopt the repository-metadata baseline in `bitty` (code-core class)

Blocked by (cross-repo, CarryCtx graph is project-local): `bitty-docs`
`CTX-0155` — accepts the canonical baseline. Do not start the required-check
changes until that standard lands.

## Context

Audit 2026-09-11. `bitty` is the de-facto reference for the Bitty family, but it
still carries class drift:

- No root `.editorconfig` (only `bitty-docs` and `bitty-website` have one).
- No `.github/CODEOWNERS` or `.github/FUNDING.yml` (org-wide decision in CTX-0155).
- Required checks: `Quality gates`, `MSRV 1.85 check`, `Windows check and test`,
  `macOS ARM64 check and test`, `Linux Wayland`, `Linux X11 (xvfb)`,
  `Analyze (rust)`, `Analyze (actions)`, `Supply chain (deny/audit)`, plus an
  extra `CodeQL` context. Confirm whether `CodeQL` is GitHub default setup
  running in parallel with the advanced `.github/workflows/codeql.yml`
  (`Analyze (...)`); if so, either remove default setup or drop the advanced
  workflow — do not keep redundant scanning.
- `.github/workflows/snapshot-source.yml` is already the shared verbatim copy.

## Scope

1. Add `.editorconfig` matching the accepted baseline.
2. Add CODEOWNERS/FUNDING if CTX-0155 adopts them.
3. Resolve the duplicate `CodeQL` required context.
4. Keep `SECURITY.md` at repo root (do not move to `.github/`).
5. Leave `.github/workflows/release.yml` untouched — it is 621 lines and product
   specific; it needs a dedicated release-rehearsal task.

## Acceptance

- CI green; `just check` and `actionlint` pass.
- Any required-check rename is applied to branch protection in the same change
  so no required context goes missing.
- No change to `release.yml`.","displayId":"CTX-0337","id":"01M28H68G4G6DT52M1K153KT16","priority":"normal","status":"ready","title":"Adopt repository-metadata baseline in bitty (code-core)"}

{"description":"Priority: P2 | Area: ipc | Labels: fix,area:ipc,P2 | Milestone: v0.1.0 | RFC: OQ-018 | Task: CTX-0320

DEFECT (live re-verification origin/main d3a6d14, CTX-0324 round2): CTX-0322 fixed the write side (new/close/focus accept and emit stable `ws:{seq}`) but `ctl workspace list` still returns bare display names, so the documented "canonical stable id across new/list/focus/close/move" contract is only half-landed.

Repro (live instance):
bitty ctl workspace list -> {"workspaces":["ws1"],...}
bitty ctl workspace new -> {"created":"ws:3",...}
bitty ctl workspace list -> {"workspaces":["ws1","ws3"],...} (bare names)
bitty ctl workspace focus ws3 -> exit 2 usage: workspace id must match ^ws:[0-9]+$
bitty ctl workspace focus ws:3 -> exit 0
So any script that reads the list cannot round-trip its ids into focus/close.

Root: crates/bitty-app/src/ctl/apply.rs:386 `workspace_names_json` serializes `runtime.workspace_names()` (display names) into result.workspaces; CTX-0322 made `new` emit `ws:{seq}` (apply.rs:410-418) and close/focus parse sequence ids. `active` also stays the positional index (apply.rs:387).

Fix: emit the canonical `ws:{seq}` id per slot in result.workspaces (and align `active`), or add a parallel ids array, so list->focus/close round-trips. Keep the human `tabline` unchanged.

Evidence: recording/ctx-0324/round2/ctl/d2-exact-repro.txt, recording/ctx-0324/round2/ctl/d2-roundtrip.txt, recording/ctx-0324/round2/logs/devtools-live-campaign.json (probe workspace:id-round-trip FAIL).
Do not fix under this task.","displayId":"CTX-0338","id":"01M28M76X1S26MFQ4WXY41ZETZ","priority":"normal","status":"ready","title":"D2 residual: ctl workspace list emits non-canonical names; list->focus round-trip broken"}

{"description":"Priority: P2 | Area: input | Labels: fix,area:input,P2 | Milestone: v0.1.0 | RFC: OQ-004 | Task: CTX-0320

DEFECT (live re-verification origin/main d3a6d14): left-click on a pane never moves keyboard focus (click-to-focus missing). With the default `mouse.focus_follows_mouse=false`, whose documented purpose is "default off preserves click-to-focus" (crates/bitty-config/src/types.rs:115-121), a click is treated only as a selection start; no code path calls Runtime::set_focus on press.

Repro (live GUI, two panes v:1|v:2, focus v:1, default config):
left-click inside v:2 -> view list still shows v:1 focused
focus v:2 via ctl, left-click inside v:1 -> still v:2 focused
Pointer events do reach bitty: the same clicks drive drag-selection (screenshot 16 vs 17 changed 282050 pixels), and hover-to-activate works when enabled (focus flips v:1<->v:2).

Root: crates/bitty-runtime/src/runtime/input.rs:538-572 selection path has no focus-on-press; `set_focus` is invoked only by hover (mouse_chrome.rs:188/223), ctl (ctl/apply.rs:378), and keymaps (chrome_keys.rs:518).

Fix: on left press (non-Shift), hit-test the pane under the cursor and set_focus before starting selection, honoring a config opt-out if desired.

Evidence: recording/ctx-0324/round2/logs/scenario3-pointer.txt, scenario3-click-reverse.txt, screenshots/11-hover-right-default.png..15-after-click-left-from-v2.png, screenshots/16-before-drag.png vs 17-after-drag-select.png.
Do not fix under this task.","displayId":"CTX-0339","id":"01M28M76Y2E7ES07BGAWGV458P","priority":"normal","status":"ready","title":"D5: left-click does not focus a pane (click-to-focus missing)"}

{"description":"Priority: P1 | Area: appearance | Labels: fix,area:appearance,P1 | Milestone: v0.1.0 | RFC: N/A | Task: TBD (this task) | GitHub: #591

Live-verification finding (ctxlive-appearance, origin/main 3eb8e0e): the shipped 30-preset theme catalog (CTX-0350) resolves correctly, and the focused/idle outline pair is applied, but the preset's terminal palette is never applied. Window background/foreground/cursor/selection and the 16 ANSI colours stay hardcoded to bitty-dark for every preset. github-light renders #1E1E2E background and bitty-dark ANSI blocks.

Cause: RuntimeConfig has no theme/palette field; config_cli::runtime_config_from_effective carries only the outline pair. bitty-render/src/grid.rs resolved_colors uses DEFAULT_FG/DEFAULT_BG, palette_rgb reads BITTY_DARK.ansi, gpu.rs clears to DEFAULT_BG; active_theme() is test-only.

Evidence: recording/ctxlive-appearance-2026-09-12/ (shots/theme-*.png, shots/ansi-*.png, VERIFY.md).

Fix: plumb the resolved preset palette (bg/fg/cursor/selection/16 ANSI) from the effective config into the renderer and clear path; keep --safe/unknown fallback on the default palette. Add a runtime palette-resolution regression test and live per-theme screenshot evidence.

Defect discovered by live verification; not currently tracked. Parent: CTX-0350.","displayId":"CTX-0355","id":"01M2AM8K3BE27MMDFJ3N9J7AAY","priority":"high","status":"ready","title":"fix(appearance): theme preset changes only the outline — terminal palette is never applied (#591)"}

{"description":"Priority: P1 | Area: appearance | Labels: fix,area:appearance,P1 | Milestone: v0.1.0 | RFC: RFC-0002/OQ-040 | Task: TBD (this task) | GitHub: #592

Live-verification finding (ctxlive-appearance, origin/main 3eb8e0e): appearance.animations.duration_ms.* and easing.* are silently ignored. The runtime PanelAnimator is always constructed with AnimationPolicy::default() ([150,120,100,200] + default curves) in bitty-runtime/src/runtime.rs (with_plugin_host_capacity and with_plugin_host). detect_panel_animations gates on self.config.animations but triggers/progress use the animator's default policy; set_animations is never called in production. The 0 ms suppression paths (enabled=false, reduced_motion=always, --safe) happen to work because the default's reduced/safe gates short-circuit.

Evidence: recording/ctxlive-appearance-2026-09-12/ (anim/open-50crop vs open-500crop identical ~115 ms fade; anim/focus-500 ~93 ms; a removed scratch runtime test proved the tracker used 150 ms for a configured 500 ms). Existing panel_animations.rs tests only use default/zero policies, so they stay green.

Fix: adopt RuntimeConfig.animations at construction (PanelAnimator::new(config.animations)); add a regression test that fails on current main for a non-default positive duration; keep live reload via set_animations. Refs CTX-0341.","displayId":"CTX-0356","id":"01M2AM8RJJW6GNZXXBFR7KHWTF","priority":"high","status":"ready","title":"fix(appearance): panel animation duration_ms/easing ignored — runtime always uses AnimationPolicy::default() (#592)"}

{"description":"fix(runtime): session-less panels share the primary grid; new workspace shows old content and routes input to the old shell. Origin: CTX-0358 investigation (m0391). GitHub Issue #593.

DEFECT (not storage): per-View PaneSession storage is independent (panes.rs:16-25,121-178; BTreeMap<ViewId,PaneSession> runtime.rs:256). The present-layer fallback in crates/bitty-runtime/src/runtime/present.rs:558-563 clones the runtime-global primary snapshot (present.rs:355) for a session-less leaf when it is focused (CTX-0234) or whenever any pane session exists (CTX-0255). Two leaves can therefore both paint the same grid.

REPRO (headless, scratch tests removed after capture; evidence in ../recording/ctx-0358/findings.md):
(1) ctl view split shape: unfocused new pane ink=false; focused session-less new pane ink=true while pane_snapshot(new)=None and primary still carries the seeded marker.
(2) mixed v1 session-less focused / v2 live / v3 session-less unfocused: both session-less leaves ink=true.
(3) workspace_new (workspaces.rs:296-325, documented lazy spawn) creates a session-less focused leaf: new leaf ink=true with old primary marker; typing reaches the previous workspace's shell (input.rs:306-324 falls back to self.pty_writer) -> GOT-HELLO echoed from old shell.

WORK:
1. Replace the snapshot.clone() fallback with an explicit bounded session-less state (erased placeholder or pending-spawn), never a clone of another pane's grid.
2. Give workspace_new a real per-leaf shell spawn so the first typed byte cannot reach another workspace's PTY.
3. Regression tests: two session-less leaves never both render primary; focusing a session-less new pane does not clone another pane's content; new workspace has its own shell and input never reaches the previous workspace's shell.

Do NOT regress CTX-0234/CTX-0255/CTX-0284 pinned behavior without updating those tests. References: kitty https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/launch/ ; ghostty https://ghostty.org/docs/config/reference.

{"description":"# fix(runtime): split after workspace_new reuses another workspace's ViewId (cross-workspace bleed)

## Summary

Live verification CTX-0365 on `origin/main` `b377820` found a P1 defect in the
workspace + split interaction. After `workspace new` creates `ws2` (fresh
`ViewId` `v:2`), returning to `ws1` and creating a split allocates the new leaf
from the **active layout's** max id + 1 instead of a globally unique id. The
split leaf reuses `v:2`, which `ws2` already owns. `pane_sessions` is keyed
globally by `ViewId` (`crates/bitty-runtime/src/runtime/panes.rs:121`
`spawn_shell_for_view`), so `ws1`'s empty split pane aliases `ws2`'s live shell:

- `ws1`'s split pane paints `ws2`'s shell content;
- typing in `ws1`'s split pane executes in `ws2`'s shell (observed PID 755182);
- `terminal list` reports the `ws1` split pane as `has_pane_session=true`;
- the keymap `new_split` path additionally spawns a shell for the colliding id,
  which replaces/drops the other session (`panes.rs:145-149`), killing `ws2`'s
  shell.

Priority: P1 | Area: runtime | Labels: fix,area:runtime,P1 | Milestone: v0.1.0 | RFC: OQ-TBD | Task: CTX-TBD

## Root cause

- `crates/bitty-app/src/ctl.rs:1770` — ctl `view split`: `next_id =` max leaf id
  of `runtime.layout()` (active layout only) `+ 1`.
- `crates/bitty-app/src/chrome_keys.rs:180` `next_view_id(layout)` and its use
  at `chrome_keys.rs:449` for the keymap `new_split` path — same active-layout
  scan.
- The correct allocator already exists:
  `crates/bitty-runtime/src/runtime/workspaces.rs:168`
  `next_view_id_global()` (max over every slot + the live layout), used by
  `workspace_new` (`workspaces.rs:296`).

## Repro (live, deterministic)

Built debug binary from `origin/main` `b377820`; isolated XDG home +
`BITTY_SOCKET`; controlled via `bitty ctl`.

1. `bitty ctl workspace new` -> `ws2` created, owns `v:2` and shell PID B.
2. `bitty ctl workspace focus ws:1` -> back on `ws1`.
3. `bitty ctl view split --right` -> `new_view=v:2` (collides with `ws2`'s `v:2`).
4. `bitty ctl terminal list` (while `ws1` active) -> `t:2 has_pane_session=true`
   (should be `false`: the split leaf has no shell of its own).
5. `bitty ctl terminal send t:2 'echo LEAK fish_pid=$fish_pid'` (while `ws1`
   focused) -> echoed with `fish_pid=B`, i.e. it ran in `ws2`'s shell.
6. `bitty ctl terminal text t:2` (while `ws1` active) -> shows `ws2`'s shell
   scrollback (its earlier markers), proving content mirroring.

`workspace new` itself (CH1) and plain switching isolation (CH2) pass; the
defect is triggered by a split while a second workspace already holds a
"next" id.

## Affected paths

| Path               | Location                 | Allocator                  |
| ------------------ | ------------------------ | -------------------------- |
| ctl `view split`   | `ctl.rs:1770-1778`       | active layout max + 1      |
| keymap `new_split` | `chrome_keys.rs:180,449` | active layout max + 1      |
| `workspace_new`    | `workspaces.rs:168,296`  | `next_view_id_global` (ok) |

## Evidence

`recording/ctx-0365/` (workspace-local, gitignored scratch):

- `results.tsv` — `CH4-view-id-collision`, `CH4-sessionless-detected`,
  `CH4-input-routing-leak`, `CH4-content-mirror` all `FAIL`.
- `evidence/shell-pids.txt` — `ws1_shell_pid=753116 ws2_shell_pid=755182`,
  `new_view=v:2 ws2_view=v:2`.
- `evidence/LEAK-ws2-shell-text.txt` — `LEAK-... fish_pid=755182` in `ws2`.
- `evidence/LEAK-ws1-split-pane.txt` / `LEAK-ws1-pane-after.txt` — `ws2`
  content displayed by `ws1`'s split pane.
- `shots/ws1-split-leak-view.png`, `shots/ws2-leak-view.png`,
  `shots/ws1-split-after.png`, `shots/LEAK-ws1-split-shows-ws2.png`.

## Proposed direction

Allocate every new split leaf with the global allocator (expose
`next_view_id_global` or add a runtime split helper that assigns the id), for
both the keymap and ctl paths. Add a regression test:
`workspace_new` -> focus `ws1` -> split -> assert the new `ViewId` is not owned
by any workspace slot, and that input sent to the split leaf never reaches
another workspace's shell.","displayId":"CTX-0378","id":"01M2CJNHCDTXCEFE4JAP86HE3V","priority":"high","status":"ready","title":"fix(runtime): split after workspace_new reuses another workspace's ViewId (cross-workspace bleed)"}

{"description":"Priority: P1 | Area: tooling | Labels: fix,area:tooling,P1 | Milestone: v0.1.0 | RFC: n/a | Task: CTX-XXXX

## Context

User directives m0549/m0552: the `recordings/` directory is a long-standing problem
(root cause: hardcoded umbrella workspace paths plus singular/plural drift), and no
absolute host paths may be committed — relative or URL references only.

## Verified state (origin/main 37ad5a8)

The original findings were generated against a stale checkout. CTX-0280 / CTX-0285 /
CTX-0296 already removed the absolute literals from
`crates/bitty-compat-lab/src/compare.rs` and `src/bin/collect_dumps.rs` (umbrella now
read from `$BITTY_WORKSPACE`), and added `scripts/check-scratch-paths.sh`, wired into
`just check`. The remaining delta is the derivation fallback, the still-plural live
references and tracked artifacts, and broader gate coverage.

## Remaining delta (this task)

1. Derivation hardening: `umbrella_root()` falls back to the parent of
   `workspace_root()` when `$BITTY_WORKSPACE` is unset (crate-relative, never an
   absolute literal). Candidate ordering stays singular before legacy plural.
   Unit tests construct expectations from the derivation helpers, plus env-override
   and parent-derivation tests.
2. De-pluralize remaining live `recordings/` references: `.gitignore`,
   `docs/product/compat-matrix.md`, `docs/product/manual-smoke.md`; delete tracked
   `recordings/README.md`, `recordings/compat-matrix-2026-09-01.json`,
   `recordings/dogfooding-evidence-2026-08-31.md`; update statements that depend on
   them. CHANGELOG.md stays untouched (historical).
3. Gate: extend `scripts/check-scratch-paths.sh` so a future `***REDACTED-PATH***`, absolute home
   path, or `recordings/` literal in tracked files fails. Add committed fixtures plus
   a runner and wire it into `just check`.
4. TDD: path-derivation tests and gate fixtures first, then the implementation.

## Scope

- `crates/bitty-compat-lab/src/lib.rs`, `src/compare.rs`, `src/bin/collect_dumps.rs`
- `scripts/check-scratch-paths.sh`, `scripts/tests/**`
- `justfile`, `.gitignore`
- `docs/product/compat-matrix.md`, `docs/product/manual-smoke.md`
- deletion of tracked `recordings/**`

## Out of scope

- `CHANGELOG.md` historical prose.
- The legacy plural fallback candidates in `compare.rs` (CR-COMPAT-01 ordering must
  keep working).

## Acceptance criteria

- `just check`, `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --locked`, and
  `cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --workspace --all-targets --locked`
  pass locally with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` set.
- No absolute host/workspace path literal in tracked files outside the gate script
  and its fixtures; no live plural `recordings/` reference outside the legacy
  fallback candidates and historical log/CHANGELOG prose.
- PR links this task, closes the Issue, and CI is green; review by a different agent.","displayId":"CTX-0379","id":"01M2CW3QC7BTXS76G2RB04DEDX","priority":"high","status":"ready","title":"fix(compat): remove absolute workspace paths and recordings/ plural drift"}

{"content":"BG-3 decision: literal peak-memory ceiling, not resident-decoded-bytes. RFC-0001 verification obligation requires a pre-allocation rejection test proving peak memory stays under BG-3, so the decode path must not allocate a second full-size buffer. Fix: replace load_from_memory_with_format().to_rgba8() (which clones even RGBA8 at image 0.25.9) with a per-format ImageDecoder that decodes into exactly one width*height*4 RGBA8 allocation, expanding L8/La8/Rgb8 channels in place. Native 16-bit and other non-8-bit decoder color types are rejected defensively (16-bit PNG already rejected at sniff). BG-2 (4096x4096) and BG-3 (64 MiB) are unchanged for all accepted formats; no accepted invariant is weakened. Regression test uses a thread-local tracking global allocator to measure peak allocation for PNG-RGBA, PNG-RGB, JPEG-RGB and WebP-RGBA at 4096x4096. Before: 8 B/px RGBA-native (128 MiB) and 7 B/px RGB-native (112 MiB). After target: <= 4 B/px plus bounded encoded input and codec scratch.","display_id":"PX-2214","id":"01M2DAP8K7KX8BHMQQ2FWAQ5NE","item_type":"note","status":"open","task_id":"01M2D7CC2NVZY5EFBK48HD6WEQ"}

{"content":"RFC-0001/OQ-042 impact needing review: to make BG-3 a literal peak guarantee for every accepted image, the pre-allocation estimate now charges 8 bytes per pixel for static WebP without a direct RGBA8 write (VP8 lossy, VP8X, and VP8L without the alpha bit), instead of the table value w*h*4. image-webp allocates a full-size internal RGBA scratch buffer when has_alpha is false (measured 8.00 B/px lossless RGB) and decoder planes for VP8 (measured 5.62 B/px lossy RGB). Consequence: a 4096x4096 non-alpha WebP is now rejected with DecodedTooLarge; its largest accepted square side is 2896. 3840x2160 (4K) lossy WebP still fits (about 63.3 MiB estimate). This is a tightening, not a weakening, but it revises the BG-3 formula for WebP and must be reflected in RFC-0001 or explicitly reverted to a codec-scratch-excluded reading. Second residual: the 8 B/px factor is derived from image-webp 0.2.4 internals and could drift on dependency upgrades; the regression test pins the measured behavior. GitHub: https://github.com/bitty-terminal/bitty/issues/905

## Defect
crates/bitty-agent/src/session.rs:267-283. In the state-machine match, the broad (SessionState::Created, _, _) arm precedes the (Running, Assistant, has-tool-calls) arm, so the FIRST accepted assistant turn with tool calls transitions Created -> Running instead of WaitingToolResult. The same accepted turn can then later be read as WaitingToolResult in mixed sequences, i.e. the resulting state is not a function of (prior state, role, tool_calls).

Note: #937's resolution comment claimed this was fixed by PR #948 (CTX-0548), but #948 is the ChildToken Debug redaction change; origin/main session.rs is still the defective version. This is the real fix.

## Fix (minimal)
Reorder/derive the transition so the assistant-with-tool-calls case is decided before the broad Created arm; (Created, Assistant, tool_calls non-empty) -> WaitingToolResult, (Created, other) -> Running. Do not change any other arm's semantics.

## Acceptance
- Pure transition tests: first assistant turn with tool calls from Created lands WaitingToolResult; pushing the tool results then lands Running; assistant without tool calls from Created lands Running; full loop is consistent.
- Existing tests untouched and green.

## Scope
